newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds climbed higher before the close on Friday, as the strong U.S. dollar fuelled activity in the afternoon by boosting the peseta versus the Deutsche mark, traders in Madrid said.
"It's mainly the dollar, which is supporting the peseta versus the mark. In general, it's sparkling optimism everywhere and so also here," a dealer at a broker house in Madrid said.
"At this point, it's possible to see the long bond future climbing once more above the 118.10, maybe also breaking it during the first days of the next week," he said.
But local dealers remained more pessimistic over the spread.
The 10-year spread versus Bunds ended virtually unchanged at 66 basis points.
"It could fall a bit but no more than to around 60 basis points," a dealer said.
The long-bond future hit a record high this week at 118.12, a level seen as very strong resistance, an analyst said.
June CPI, which accelerated to 1.6 percent year on year from a 1.5-percent rise in May. had little impact on prices. The rise was as expected.
